# k0rdent_kubernetes_cluster (Data Source)

One Kubernetes cluster, read rather than managed.

Use it to reference a cluster another configuration owns, without taking ownership of it. It carries more than the `k0rdent_kubernetes_cluster` resource does: health, the control plane's state, the platform's state message and the current operation all change without the configuration changing, so the resource cannot carry them without reporting drift on every refresh, and a read-only form can.

An upgrade in progress shows as `upgrade_target_version_id`, with its phase and start time under `operation`.

It does not return the control plane's CA certificate yet. The `k0rdent_cluster_kubeconfig` ephemeral resource carries it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Read a cluster another configuration owns, without managing it.

data "k0rdent_kubernetes_cluster" "training" {
  id = "ml-training"

  # Both default to the provider's scope. Name them to read a cluster in
  # another region or project.
  # region  = "us-texas-1"
  # project = "cp-production"
}

# Health, control plane state and the current operation are only here, not on
# the resource.
output "is_degraded" {
  value = data.k0rdent_kubernetes_cluster.training.health_state != "healthy"
}

# An upgrade's progress, or null when none is running. try() gives null when
# there's no operation.
output "upgrade" {
  value = data.k0rdent_kubernetes_cluster.training.upgrade_target_version_id == null ? null : {
    target        = data.k0rdent_kubernetes_cluster.training.upgrade_target_version_id
    stage         = try(data.k0rdent_kubernetes_cluster.training.operation.current_stage, null)
    percent       = try(data.k0rdent_kubernetes_cluster.training.operation.percent_complete, null)
    started_at    = try(data.k0rdent_kubernetes_cluster.training.operation.started_at, null)
    control_plane = data.k0rdent_kubernetes_cluster.training.control_plane_message
  }
}

# Warn in the plan if the cluster isn't active. A check doesn't stop the run.
# coalesce() fills in text for a null state or message.
check "cluster_is_up" {
  assert {
    condition     = data.k0rdent_kubernetes_cluster.training.state == "active"
    error_message = "Cluster ml-training is ${coalesce(data.k0rdent_kubernetes_cluster.training.state, "in no reported state")}: ${coalesce(data.k0rdent_kubernetes_cluster.training.state_message, "no reason given")}."
  }
}

# The API server URL. For the CA certificate, use the ephemeral kubeconfig.
output "api_endpoint" {
  value = data.k0rdent_kubernetes_cluster.training.api_endpoint
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) The cluster's name, which is its id. **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL.

### Optional

- `project` (String) Project to read. Defaults to the provider's `project`. **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL.
- `region` (String) Region to read. Defaults to the provider's `region`. **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL.

### Read-Only

- `api_endpoint` (String) URL of the Kubernetes API server. Null until the control plane has one. The certificate to trust it with is not returned here; see the `k0rdent_cluster_kubeconfig` ephemeral resource.
- `cluster_type` (String) The ClusterType version this cluster is bound to, as the platform reports it. Normally the pinned `/versions/{id}` form even where an unversioned reference was supplied at creation.
- `cluster_type_name` (String) Display name of the bound ClusterType version, as of binding.
- `control_plane_desired_replicas` (Number) Control plane replicas the hosted control plane's spec asks for. Null whenever `control_plane_state` is.
- `control_plane_message` (String) Why `control_plane_state` is what it is. Free text to show, not to parse. Null whenever `control_plane_state` is.
- `control_plane_ready_replicas` (Number) Control plane replicas passing their readiness probe, to read against `control_plane_desired_replicas`. Null whenever `control_plane_state` is, and a 0 here is a real reading.
- `control_plane_state` (String) The platform's judgement of a hosted control plane: `ready`, `provisioning`, `progressing`, `degraded`, `unavailable`, `deleting` or `unknown`. `ready` means the tenant API server answers. `progressing` covers both a scale and a version rollout; compare `control_plane_version` with the bound ClusterType version to tell them apart. Null until a hosted control plane has been observed, and always null on a standalone one.
- `control_plane_version` (String) The version the hosted control plane is actually running. It lags the bound ClusterType version while an upgrade rolls out. Empty until a replica is ready, and null whenever `control_plane_state` is.
- `description` (String) Free-form text describing it, for people to read.
- `display_name` (String) Human-friendly name, for display only.
- `health_reason` (String) Why the health is what it is. Null when healthy.
- `health_state` (String) Observed health, which is reported separately from `state` and never drives it. `unknown` until the platform first reports it.
- `kubernetes_version` (String) The Kubernetes version the bound ClusterType version carries, such as `v1.35.1+k0s.0`, read from that version's `k8s.k0sVersion`. It's the version the cluster is bound to: `control_plane_version` is what a hosted control plane runs, and lags it while an upgrade rolls out. Null when the bound version carries no Kubernetes configuration, or the platform no longer finds it.
- `next_available_cluster_type_version` (String) The ClusterType version this cluster could move to, when one is available. Null when it is on the latest.
- `node_count` (Number) Total nodes across every pool the cluster has.
- `node_pools` (Attributes Map) Every pool the platform created, including the ones a configuration did not name, keyed by pool slug: the same key a cluster's `node_pool` map uses. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--node_pools))
- `operation` (Attributes) The cluster's current or last lifecycle operation: a create, a scale, an upgrade or a delete. This is where an upgrade's phase and start time are read. Null on a cluster that has never run one. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--operation))
- `security_groups` (List of String) Security groups applied to the cluster's instances. Order is significant: it is the order the fabric applies them in.
- `self_link` (String) Platform-defined reference to this cluster.
- `state` (String) Lifecycle state. `active` is settled and usable.
- `state_message` (String) The platform's own explanation of the current state. Null when there is nothing to explain.
- `state_reason` (String) Machine-readable cause of a `failed` state, such as `INSUFFICIENT_CAPACITY`. Stable enough to branch on, unlike `state_message`. Null when no failure is recorded.
- `tags` (Map of String) User-defined labels, as key-value pairs.
- `upgrade_target_version_id` (String) Id of the ClusterType version an upgrade in flight is moving to. Null when no upgrade is in flight. On success `cluster_type` moves to it; on failure this is cleared and `cluster_type` stays where it was.

<a id="nestedatt--node_pools"></a>
### Nested Schema for `node_pools`

Read-Only:

- `display_name` (String) Display name, resolved from the ClusterType's pool.
- `node_count` (Number) Settled number of nodes in the pool.
- `target_node_count` (Number) Desired count while a scale is in flight. Null when the pool is idle, in which case `node_count` is the whole story.


<a id="nestedatt--operation"></a>
### Nested Schema for `operation`

Read-Only:

- `completed_at` (String) When the operation ended, in RFC 3339. Null while it runs, and also on an operation older than the field, so read `status` to know whether it is still going.
- `current_stage` (String) Key of the stage in progress, else the stage that failed, else the next one pending, such as `reserving-hardware`. Null when none applies.
- `execution_id` (String) Identifier of the operation, stable for its lifetime. Quote it when asking the platform team what happened.
- `message` (String) The platform's own detail about the operation. Read it, do not branch on it.
- `percent_complete` (Number) Share of the operation's stages done or skipped, rounded down. Null when the platform reports no stages.
- `reason` (String) Machine-readable cause, such as `TIMEOUT`. Stable enough to branch on. Null when none is recorded.
- `started_at` (String) When the operation began, in RFC 3339. Subtract it from `plantimestamp()` for how long it has been running. Null on an operation older than the field.
- `status` (String) `running`, `succeeded`, `failed` or `cancelled`. Not final: a cluster the platform force-failed can still converge and move this back to `succeeded`.
